notes: ACCESS: HTTP-FIRST tier used throughout. robots.txt (www.target.com) checked first - blanket 'User-agent: * / Disallow:' block list does not cover /c/ category paths and names no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web disallow, so tier (a) was permitted. Tier (a) plain curl fetch of www.target.com/c/... pages succeeded (200 OK, no impersonation needed) and returned a server-rendered __NEXT_DATA__ JSON blob containing the full category/breadcrumb tree (used for TREE below) - this is reliable and fast. However the live per-category PRODUCT COUNT is not present in that server-rendered payload; it loads client-side via Target's redsky plp_search_v2 API. A direct tier-(a) HTTP call to that API (with the public key embedded in the page JS) returned 403 (Varnish-cached Forbidden) even with Referer/Origin headers - first block on that host for that specific need. Escalated to tier (b): Playwright (headless and headful) loaded the category pages but the plp_search_v2 XHR the page itself fired either hung indefinitely (page stuck on 'Loading...' skeletons) or (once) returned a captcha challenge payload - tier (b) also could not reliably surface the count. Escalated to tier (c): Claude-in-Chrome (the user's real Chrome profile) successfully rendered every category page and exposed the 'N results' heading through the accessibility tree (via the find tool) after normal client-side load (typically 5-40s per page, occasionally 2 attempts) - this matches the memory note that Target's redsky-backed count is reliable once actually rendered. All 139 qty values in this file are exact numbers read this way (each evidence string cites the page URL); qty was never estimated/aggregated. QTY: see evidence field per leaf row for method; all leaves report the exact 'N results' heading Target itself renders on that category's own listing page (deepest valid node per URL, not a parent total). TREE: built from union of (1) the Home & Decor mega-menu top-level children (root node N-5xtvd, 20 children) obtained via tier (a) __NEXT_DATA__, (2) each relevant child category's own __NEXT_DATA__ 'children' array recursed down to leaf nodes (children:0), covering Bedding, Bath, Rugs, Window Treatments, Storage & Organization, Home Decor > Decorative Pillows & Blankets / Couch & Furniture Covers, Kitchen & Dining > Kitchen & Table Linens / Kitchen Storage & Organization, and the Kids' Home cross-links into those same categories - no separate sub-nav or sitemap divergence was found beyond this __NEXT_DATA__ tree, so it was treated as authoritative. Grouping rows follow the site's own hierarchy (parent group immediately followed by its children in reading order per textile.md Sec.26 / storage.md Sec.44); duplicate leaf nodes reachable from two parents in Target's own menu (e.g. Throw Pillows under both Bedding>Bed & Support Pillows and Home Decor>Decorative Pillows & Blankets; Kids' Rugs under both Rugs and Kids' Decor; Kitchen Rugs & Mats under both Rugs and Kitchen & Table Linens) were recorded exactly once, under the grouping judged most specific, per the duplicate-URL rule. EXCLUDED: Deals/Clearance/New Arrivals/Bestsellers/Buying-Guide/Registry/'Dorm' cross-category landing pages (View-All/Collection rule); hardware (curtain rods/rails/hooks/rings, shower-curtain rods & hooks, window-treatment hardware); Bathroom Furniture, Bathroom Mirrors, Bathroom Scales, and all non-storage Bathroom Accessories (soap dishes/dispensers, tissue box covers, toothbrush holders, canisters, trays, tumblers, makeup mirrors, towel warmers, wastebaskets/trash cans - trash cans excluded storage-wide, not on the include list); Trash Cans & Recycling Bins (all locations); Car Organizers (automotive, not home storage); Hooks subtree (hardware, not storage); Floating Shelves and Letter Boards (Target's own canonical URL places these under Wall Decor, out of scope); Bookshelves & Bookcases (canonical URL contains 'office-furniture', Furniture-task boundary); Poufs (Furniture); Charger Plates, Napkin Rings, Party Tablecloths (Kitchen & Dining tableware/party-supplies, not genuine textile); Butter Dishes & Keepers, Oil & Syrup Dispensers, Sugar Bowls (canonical URLs place these under Serveware, not Food Storage, despite cross-listing on the Food Storage page); Food Storage Accessories subtree (bag clips/food covers/scoops/lids - kitchen tools, not storage containers themselves) and Travel & To-Go Food Containers subtree (lunch boxes, bento boxes, travel mugs, picnic baskets - portable Kitchen & Dining items, not home storage) and Canning Jars/Tools & Supplies (canonical under Kitchen Utensils & Gadgets); Sink Accessories subtree (dish drying mats/racks, over-the-sink racks, sponge holders - functional kitchen accessories, not storage); Napkin Holders, Paper Towel Holders, Cookbook & Recipe Holders, Spoon Rests (functional/display kitchen accessories, not storage); Horizontal Blinds and Mini Blinds (hard aluminum/wood slat blinds, not textile/fabric per textile.md's material test - Cellular/Roller/Roman/Tie-Up Shades were kept as fabric-based); Tub & Shower Mats (rubber/vinyl safety mat, not textile fabric); Rug Pads (accessory/underlay, parallel to the curtain-rod hardware exclusion); Bath Toys, Potty Training, Kids' Bath Accessories, Kids' Decorative Accents & Accessories (generic/non-textile kids items); Bed Planner and Rugs Buying Guide (interactive tools/guides, not product categories); The Disney and Marvel Collections by Pillowfort and Weighted Stuffed Animals (character-brand collection page / toy, not textile); Clean Sleep (mattress-care marketing collection page); Gift & Occasion Baskets (gift assortment, not storage); Jewelry Storage is cross-listed by Target under Clothing/Jewelry & Watches rather than Home & Decor > Storage & Organization but was kept (MEDIUM confidence) since it is a genuine storage/organizer product line reached from the Storage & Organization menu. Kids' Lamps & Lighting, Kids' Night Lights, Kids' Piggy Banks, Kids' Wall Decor, all Wall Decor/Decorative Accents/Mirrors/Clocks/Candles/Artificial Plants nodes, Furniture and Furniture-Kitchen-Dining nodes, Heating/Cooling, Vacuums, Home Appliances, Automotive, Home Improvement, Outdoor Living & Garden (non-rug/non-storage), and Teen Room > Furniture/Lighting were out of scope per the ruleset boundary sections and skipped entirely (neither array). LOW-confidence rows (Wedges & Positioners, Storage Furniture, Kids' Shelving & Bookcases, Fruit Baskets & Holders) are flagged MANUAL REVIEW in their flag field per-row with the specific ambiguity.
